question: Examine whether the equations $3x-2y=5$ and $6x-4y=13$ can have a common solution. Give mathematical justification.
explanation:
Comparison of variable coefficients
The corresponding coefficient ratios are $$\frac{3}{6}=\frac{-2}{-4}=\frac{1}{2}$$
Comparison of constants
The ratio of the constants is $$\frac{5}{13}$$ which is not equal to $\frac{1}{2}$.
Inconsistency condition
The variable coefficients are proportional, but the constants are not proportional. Equivalently, multiplying the first equation by $2$ gives $6x-4y=10$, which contradicts $6x-4y=13$.
Conclusion
Therefore, no ordered pair can satisfy both equations simultaneously. Hence, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.A: The equations have infinitely many common solutions because all corresponding coefficients are proportional.
options.B: The equations have a unique common solution because their constants are unequal.
options.C: The equations have the common solution $(1,-1)$.
options.D: The system is inconsistent and has no common solution because the variable coefficients are proportional but the constants are not.
